To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a new method for matching multiple observations of a moving vehicle that is not limited to contiguous frames and can handle changes in pose, appearance and aspect ratio across the observations.
we have shown that the use of vehicle fingerprinting can be successfully employed for vehicle tracking in videos.

we have developed a vehicle matching method that can match two sequences of vehicle observations separated in time, even though the two sequences do not overlap in time and are separated by a significant time gap.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of vehicle tracking from multiple aerial platforms where the vehicles are moving in an environment and are imaged from multiple viewpoints.
developing algorithms for vehicle reacquisition in videos that can be used in the context of tracking multiple vehicles in a scene.
the problem of reacquisition tracking of objects from multiple observations that are separated in time and not contiguous.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current work has shown the feasibility of vehicle fingerprinting and re-acquisition for vehicle tracking from aerial video.
the proposed method performs well for the problem of vehicle tracking from a moving aerial platform, but it is still not clear whether it will perform as well for other domains.

the current work is the first attempt in the literature that uses the concept of vehicle fingerprinting and quasi rigid alignment in a comprehensive and unified manner for the problem of tracking vehicles from aerial platforms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to achieve 100% accuracy in matching sequences from the same vehicle with 99.9% accuracy for sequences from different vehicles.
the proposed approach is able to match two or more sequences with a high degree of confidence and can also be applied to other domains of tracking.
the proposed method is robust and effective to the problem of vehicle reacquisition tracking.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed framework can handle significant changes in appearance and pose and is robust enough to be used in real world applications.
the use of vehicle fingerprints can significantly improve the performance of vehicle reacquisition in videos.
the vehicle fingerprinting approach can be applied to any object tracking problem where multiple observations are separated by significant time intervals.
